record.paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
record.context_brief: Periodic commutative embeddings into Abelian power semigroups
record.original_question: Determine whether every periodic commutative semigroup embeds into the power semigroup over a periodic Abelian group.

evidence.quote:
Problem 5.3. (S.G. Bershadsky, S.I. Kublanovsky) Is every periodic commutative semigroup em-
beddable into the power semigroup over a periodic Abelian group?
           This is true for all regular commutative semigroups and for some finite non-regular com-
mutative semigroups (see [3]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a group (or semigroup) $G$, let $\mathcal{P}(G)$ denote the power semigroup of $G$: the set of all nonempty subsets of $G$ equipped with the multiplication
$$A \cdot B = \{ab : a \in A,\ b \in B\}.$$
A semigroup $S$ is called periodic if for every $s \in S$ there exist positive integers $m \neq n$ with $s^m = s^n$ (equivalently, every monogenic subsemigroup of $S$ is finite). A group $G$ is periodic if every element has finite order.

Question: Does every periodic commutative semigroup $S$ embed (as a semigroup) into $\mathcal{P}(G)$ for some periodic Abelian group $G$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is recorded as an unsolved problem in a recent compilation of open questions in semigroup theory (Lyapin's notebook). It is known to hold for all regular commutative semigroups and for some finite non-regular commutative semigroups, but the general case appears to remain open.
